title: The Blue Beetle
paragraphs: Short-lived 1940 juvenile superhero/crime serial adapted from the Blue Beetle comic-book property.
The run breaks into several distinct periods: 1940 syndicated Blue Beetle serial (May 15, 1940 to September 13, 1940).

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include [[person|frank-lovejoy|Frank Lovejoy]] (performer), Paul Ford (performer), Charles Nicholas (creator (for all shows)) (performer), and Jean Grombach (performer).

The stories often return to organized crime and protection rackets, kidnapping, captivity and rescue, crime-fighting gadgets and speculative technology, police work and extra-legal crime fighting, robbery, payroll theft and stolen valuables, and sabotage, espionage and subversion.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Comic-book superhero moves into radio, Juvenile adventure serial culture, Prewar sabotage and spy-story motifs, and Flexible syndicated presentation formats.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|boston-blackie|Boston Blackie]], [[show|box-13|Box 13]], [[show|columbia-workshop|Columbia Workshop]], [[show|escape|Escape]], and [[show|lights-out|Lights Out]].
